Subject: Redwood update — brief on this morning's latency event affecting Asteria production

Liam / Asteria team,

Thanks for your patience — quick update from Redwood on the event we began investigating at 07:58 PT this morning.

What happened (high level):
- Starting ~07:58 PT, we saw a sustained increase in 95th percentile inference latency for your production workload against model-rw-7b. This caused some client-side retries and elevated response times.
- No inference results were lost and no customer data was exposed.

What we did:
- Opened an incident bridge and identified a recent routing change that increased load on a degraded node pool. We rolled back that routing configuration at ~08:05 PT and rebalanced traffic.
- We increased the autoscaler headroom for your dedicated pool and applied a temporary routing fallback to older model-weight shards to reduce tail latency while the bridge worked through remediation.

Customer impact:
- A subset of requests (estimated <0.8% of overall calls) experienced elevated latency (p95 ~3.2s) for ~7 minutes. Most requests returned within normal bounds after rollback.

Next steps:
- We will produce a postmortem and share it by EOD tomorrow (Nov 21) with a root-cause analysis and corrective actions.
- We are proposing a short-term configuration change to your routing policy to prevent recurrence; Dev will follow up with the exact config and rollout plan.
- If you need an on-call call now, we can join — otherwise we will send the postmortem and a remediation timeline.

Attachments (high level): severity-snapshot.png

Apologies for the disruption — we know latency is sensitive for your workflows. Please let me know if you'd like an immediate bridge or prefer the postmortem timeline.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:11:00 -0800
Subject: Postmortem plan and artifacts for Asteria event (RI-2345)

Follow-up internal notes:
- Root cause hypothesis: a canary routing tweak deployed at 07:44 PT caused uneven distribution to a node pool that had elevated kernel scheduler contention following a low-frequency maintenance job. The maintenance job overlapped earlier and pushed one node's latency into the tail.
- Evidence: traces (trace ids included in Drive link), autoscaler logs showing a transient scale-down, and the routing-change diff.

Planned corrective actions:
- Short-term: pin routing policy to stable profile and disable the canary for Asteria until we validate scheduler behavior across the pool. (ETA: 2 hours from now for config rollout)
- Medium-term: improve autoscaler safety margins and add a synthetic steady-state traffic test before routing canary promotion.
- Postmortem deliverable: draft shared in Drive (postmortem-draft.docx). I will prepare the RCA and proposed mitigation items; Grace will own post-deployment verification steps.

Action items assigned: Dev: RCA + draft (due EOD today), Grace: verification playbook + regression tests, Aditya: approve customer-facing postmortem and SLA exception request.

--
Dev Patel
SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Final update and next steps — Asteria production latency event (Nov 20)

Liam / team,

Following our bridge and the investigation, here is the executive summary and what to expect next:

Executive summary:
- Impact window: ~07:58–08:06 PT on Nov 20.
- Symptom: transient p95 latency increase (peaked ~3.2s) affecting ~0.8% of requests; no data loss.
- Immediate remediation: rolled back routing canary; increased autoscaler headroom and applied routing fallback.

Committed deliverables:
- Postmortem with RCA and timeline for remediation (we will share the draft by EOD today and final by end of day Nov 22).
- Proposed SLA exception request (attached) to document the event and next steps; we will submit if you approve.
- A verification run: we will execute the regression tests and synthetic steady-state traffic test in a staging slot and share results before re-enabling canary.

If this approach works for you, please reply with your sign-off on the SLA exception and whether you prefer a short sync (15m) early next week to review the postmortem draft.

Thanks again for working through this with us — we take these incidents very seriously and will follow up with a complete RCA and timeline for the preventative changes.

Best regards,
Aditya Rao
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
